_why: THE NEXT 2+1 — the anchor-slide book with ONE lever moved: the INPUT LADDER becomes an explicit per-era list, 1 / 1.5 / 2.6 / 4.7, in place of geometric B 1.5^era (1 / 1.5 / 2.25 / 3.375). Everything else is byte-identical to probe-anch-costslide: the same eight-industry e1 anchor slide, --anchor-cost, in0 1.2, A 2.2, C 1.9, the same ai_value ladder, ai_defines and 24-month bar. The ECONOMIC field diff is `inputs` on 22 rungs and nothing else; target_be and wage_pct also differ, but only because this book is generated on the measured-wage basis of 2026-09-20 (§10.87) while probe-anch-costslide predates it — neither is emitted as economics (target_be is the building NAME, wage_pct is model-only).
_the_lever: A NON-GEOMETRIC input ladder, which is the axis the user's 2026-09-19 ruling explicitly OPENED ('vanilla values + uniform ladders and penalties stay, although ladders can be more complex than anchor*A^era'). It is still UNIFORM across industries — one list, every industry — so it does not reopen the per-industry axis the same ruling CLOSED. Implemented 2026-09-20 as make_ab_config's --in-ladder, the exact counterpart of the existing --cost-ladder, recorded as `_ab.in_ladder` and re-derived by L31 (proven both ways by sabotage: stripping the record fails 22 rungs, hand-editing one e3 input fails that rung by name).
_what_it_is_for: probe-anch-costslide is OUT on one broken run: GBR in CAPITAL ABUNDANCE in run 2 (U* under 5% for six consecutive years 1931-1936 at a mean hoard of 2.46 of its own GDP), with run 1 missing the identical line by one year. F135's mechanism says the pool's INFLOW is our margins, which run at twice vanilla's. BALANCE_FRAMEWORK §10.86.4 / F141 measured that an ACCELERATING input ladder is the only lever that cuts the FRONTIER's margin without touching F97's death test — the test is a ratio of VALUE ADDED between rungs two apart, so raising the top rung's inputs moves numerator and denominator together, where a lower A moves only the numerator. Verified on the two real books, slide included: the death test is 24/24 in BOTH.
_measured_from_the_books: At base prices, computed from the emitted books themselves (NOT from ladder_options, which does not model the anchor slide): mean value added per TOP-rung level 10,892 -> 9,789 (x0.899); the unslid industries' median e3 goods margin 360% -> 230%; PAPER, which the user singled out, 426% -> 277% at e3 and 259% -> 210% at e2; F97 death test 24/24 unchanged; capital per unit of output UNCHANGED (building_cost is untouched, so ROADMAP step 8's P8 build-time complaint does not move); the 1836 anchor UNCHANGED (e0 and e1 input value are identical, so F137's +27.3% over-production is exactly as before).
_why_it_lands_on_paper: Not a per-industry lever, and not an accident. The anchor slide put the eight industries whose 1836 mass sits on e1 one ladder index lower, so THEIR top rung reads index 2 (x2.6) while the unslid nine read index 3 (x4.7). The acceleration therefore lands hardest on exactly the industries that were never shifted down and whose top rungs stayed fattest - paper, art_academy, arms, motor, explosives. Input value moves x1.000 / x1.000 / x1.155 / x1.393 for the unslid set and x1.000 / x1.000 / x1.000 / x1.156 for the slid one.

_predictions._basis: THE CRITERIA REGISTER (BALANCE_FRAMEWORK §10.83). Stated before launch, as the no-ceteris-paribus rule requires. These are DIRECTIONS with magnitudes and the magnitudes are the weak half. ⚠ §10.86.2: a base-price margin is a DESIGN COORDINATE, never a prediction — F139 measured the market compressing a designed 5/55/127/233 into a realised 26/31/47/46, so do not expect the designed cuts above to appear as realised ones.
_predictions.world_gdp: 0.88-1.05 (probe-anch-costslide read 0.97 / 1.22). Value added per frontier level is x0.899, which should pull the high seed down toward the aim. THE RISK: F128's B 1.8 gain-matched STALLED at 0.70, and its lesson was that a base-price gain match UNDERSTATES the price channel (realised 0.54-0.91 against a planned 0.77-0.80). x0.899 is deliberately far short of that, but the understatement could still bite.
_predictions.pool_H: 2.2-3.0 (was 3.49). The hoard is the largest single block of the loss and the one this batch is aimed at.
_predictions.capital_abundance: THE KEY LINE: no shortlist member of 50M+ under 5% U* for five consecutive years ending by 1936 at a mean hoard >= 1.5 GDP. probe-anch-costslide broke it in run 2 and missed it by one year in run 1.
_predictions.T0: unchanged - the ladder is identical at e0 and e1, so nothing about the old rung's economics moves.
_predictions.PI: 0.82-0.92 (was 0.85). Dearer inputs per unit of output raise building-input demand, which pushes PI UP; above 1.0 the lever has overshot.

_stop_rule: THE RUN-LEVEL STOP applies (2+1 batch): a run ending above x1.3 of vanilla's 1936 GDP median is the config's last. Arm stop_watch.mjs at launch — it reads the register's HARD lines, and F151's lesson is to read those BEFORE alignment_check, because one broken run ends the config however well the seeds agree.
_third_run: only on divergence under F114's bands (GDP >= 0.15 apart AND in different bands, or workers >= 0.10 apart AND in different bands).

_branches.stalled_below_0.85: the milder sibling config/mod_config.probe-b16-slide.json (flat B 1.6: value added per top level x0.937, paper e3 333%), already generated and dry-run built clean, with its own schedule b16_slide_n2.json.
_branches.hoard_unmoved: C 2.0 on top of this ladder — the pool-ABSORPTION lever, which F135 measured as the only one that takes the hoard down while also taking W down (1.73% of hoard per 1% of world GDP).
_branches.paper_still_fat: the graded era-0 penalty (--in0-stage), which gives paper 1.30 against the flat 1.20. It needs the generator's --anchor-for / --in0-stage conflict lifted first, and ROADMAP step 10 records that as the standing blocker.
